Senya, where did you get such a beauty?
Oh, I earned this with my own wit!
What will you do with the spoiled fish?
I threw it out.
Can you give it to me?
Five hundred rubles.
What do you mean five hundred rubles?
You were going to throw it out!
Now a demand for it has appeared.
Take it, it is a good fish.
It just spoiled a little.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'еврюга'). Common feminine noun meaning 'stellate sturgeon' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас севрюга в меню появилась?
examples.trans: Did stellate sturgeon appear on our menu?
I have never eaten stellate sturgeon.

examples.text: Новый заказ: севрюга в белом вине.
examples.trans: New order: stellate sturgeon in white wine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('own, proper').

examples.text: Тогда я проведу собственное расследование и найду вора.
examples.trans: Then I will conduct my own investigation and find the thief.
Stellate sturgeon, in person!

examples.text: О, это я заработал собственным умом!
examples.trans: Oh, I earned this with my own wit!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'person' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Stellate sturgeon, in person!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть персона.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always person.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You are already almost not my husband.

examples.text: Я не собираюсь перед тобой отчитываться.
examples.trans: I am not going to report to you.
Olive oil, two bottles.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Lyova, where is the fish?
Buzz off! Where is Katya?

examples.text: Сеня, ты где такую красоту взял?
examples.trans: Senya, where did you get such a beauty?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: After all, a child needs a father.

examples.text: Скажите ему, в законе такого нет.
examples.trans: Tell him there is no such thing in the law.

examples.text: Я больше не буду так, клянусь.
examples.trans: I will not do that anymore, I swear.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'beauty' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сеня, ты где такую красоту взял?
examples.trans: Senya, where did you get such a beauty?
A beauty salon.
How beautiful!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'took', paired with 'брать'.

examples.trans: Denis, where did you come from?

examples.text: Сеня, ты где такую красоту взял?
examples.trans: Senya, where did you get such a beauty?
Go and hire Galileo.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The groom may kiss the bride.
Am I not late?
After all, a child needs a father.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It was your cook who dumped her!

examples.text: С этого момента я беру её под контроль.
examples.trans: From this moment I am taking her under my control.

examples.text: Это ты пытался украсть за эту неделю.
examples.trans: This is what you tried to steal this week.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Am I not late?

examples.text: Я не собираюсь перед тобой отчитываться.
examples.trans: I am not going to report to you.

examples.text: С этого момента я беру её под контроль.
examples.trans: From this moment I am taking her under my control.

meanings.en: to start working, to come on
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'earned', paired with 'зарабатывать'.

examples.text: О, это я заработал собственным умом!
examples.trans: Oh, I earned this with my own wit!
Oh, it's working!
He earned a lot of money.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'wit / mind' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Everything smells nice, even the paper.
Well done, Victoria thought everything through.

examples.text: Я тут подумал, мы с тобой редко видимся.
examples.trans: I was thinking here, you and I rarely see each other.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'павший'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('missing / lost').

examples.trans: And so, the missing stellate sturgeon is found.
What will you do with the spoiled fish?
The cooks were looking for the missing ingredients.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Рыба дорогая, должна быть в идеальном состоянии.
examples.trans: The fish is expensive, it must be in perfect condition.
Go work, the fish is for guests.
Lyova, where is the fish?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не понимаю, откуда такое желание завести семью?
examples.trans: I do not understand where such a desire to start a family comes from.
Let us go out somewhere.
Sure, where to?

meanings.en: to put, do with, dispose of (colloquial)
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will put / do with', paired with 'девать'.

examples.trans: Are there witnesses?
Will you have live music?

examples.text: Наташенька, у вас будет чудесная весёлая свадьба.
examples.trans: Natashenka, you will have a wonderful, merry wedding.

meanings.en: to throw out, to toss out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'кинуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to throw out', paired with 'выкидывать'.

examples.trans: I threw them into the trash bin.

examples.text: Это мэр, которого из окна выкинули!
examples.trans: This is the mayor whom they threw out of the window!
I accidentally threw out the needed paper.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'give, hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.trans: Can you give it to me?
Give me the keys.
He will hand over the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Five hundred rubles.
What do you mean five hundred rubles?
It costs five hundred roubles.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rubles' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Five hundred rubles.
What do you mean five hundred rubles?
This costs a hundred roubles.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Даже если и он, то что?
examples.trans: Even if it is him, then what?
I will think of something.

examples.text: Пап, ты уверен, что это то самое место?
examples.trans: Dad, are you sure that this is the right place?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она мне даже не сказала, кто отец ребёнка.
examples.trans: She did not even tell me who the child's father is.

examples.text: А ты знаешь, сколько она стоит?
examples.trans: And do you know how much it costs?
On the contrary, she is smart.

meanings.en: to throw out, to toss out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'кидывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw out', paired with 'выкинуть'.

examples.trans: You were going to throw it out!

examples.text: Серьёзных людей из окна не выкидывают!
examples.trans: Serious people don't get thrown out of a window!
Don't throw out these old newspapers.

meanings.en: to intend, plan, get ready to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got ready, planned', paired with 'собираться'.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?
examples.trans: Are you planning to leave me or what?
We got ready for vacation.
Are you planning to drink alcohol?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Сейчас мы проверим, гоню я или нет.
examples.trans: Right now we will check whether I am talking nonsense or not.
You will see everything for yourself right now.
I will find out everything right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Муж имеет право знать, кто отец ребёнка.
examples.trans: A husband has the right to know who the child's father is.
Shrimp, one pack.
Maybe he needs to be treated?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'прос'). Common masculine noun meaning 'demand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Now a demand for it has appeared.
Don't take other people's things without asking.
There is high demand for these flats.

meanings.en: to appear, to show up, to turn up
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'явиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to appear, to show up', paired with 'появляться'.

examples.text: Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: Let him just show up here one more time!
We came up with a good idea.

examples.text: Я тебе серьёзно говорю. Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: I'm telling you seriously. Let him just show up here one more time!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.text: Из одного брака в другой без паузы.
examples.trans: From one marriage into another without a pause.
Take your hand off!

examples.text: Заходил, но я камбалу брал, а севрюгу нет.
examples.trans: I went in, but I took flounder, not stellate sturgeon.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.trans: He is a good specialist.
Take it, it is a good fish.
A good day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У меня только эти штуки для свежего дыхания.
examples.trans: I only have these things for fresh breath.

examples.text: Тут точно рыба, только она воняет!
examples.trans: There really is a fish here, only it stinks!
It just spoiled a little.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It just spoiled a little.
I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

meanings.en: to spoil, go bad, deteriorate (of food or things)
meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'went bad / spoiled'.

examples.trans: I thought that the groceries had spoiled.
I thought that they had spoiled.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('great').

examples.trans: What a great day today.

examples.text: Отлично, теперь и свадьбы не будет.
examples.trans: Great, now there will not be a wedding either.
That turned out to be a great deal.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'deal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Всё ясно, сделаем на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Everything is clear, we will do it at the highest level.

examples.text: Следствие набрало достаточно фактов, чтобы сделать выводы.
examples.trans: The investigation has gathered enough facts to draw conclusions.
What did you do?

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turned out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.trans: It will all work out!
He'll make a good doctor.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.
